claim: KL to Taman Negara bus+boat combo via Kuala Tembeling jetty; boat registers ~12:00-12:30, departs 13:00, arrives Kuala Tahan ~16:00; 2.5-3hr river cruise; ~RM140-150.
quote: boats departing at 1300 hours and arriving at Kuala Tahan at 1600 hours... the scenic jungle river cruise takes around 2.5-3 hours

claim: Han Travel KL-Kuala Tahan with boat: RM150/ticket, departs KL 08:30, river cruise 13:00, arrives Kuala Tahan ~15:30-16:00, ~7.5hr total.
quote: RM 150.00 / Ticket... Departs: 08:30 AM from Kuala Lumpur... 1300 hours River cruise trip to Taman Negara... arrival at Kuala Tahan at 15:30

claim: Afternoon-only Kuala Tembeling boat departs 13:00-13:30; the morning boat was cancelled in 2014; KL shuttle bus to Kuala Tahan departs ~08:30.
quote: 1PM - 1.30PM departure... Morning boat had been cancelled in year 2014

claim: Park admission RM1, camera permit RM5; canopy walkway RM5 (530m, at foot of Bukit Teresek); direct road from KL ~3.5hr; Bukit Teresek, canopy walk and Lubuk Simpon reachable on foot; floating restaurants line Kuala Tahan riverside.
quote: Canopy Walkway... Cost: RM5... Park Fees: Admission costs RM1; camera permit RM5... The 3.5 hr driving route bypasses the scenic river boat

claim: Cameron Highlands to Taman Negara minivan+river boat combo takes ~5-6hr including Jerantut stop and longboat to Kuala Tahan.
quote: The total travel time is around 5-6 hours, including the minivan transfer from Cameron Highlands, a short stop in Jerantut, and the river boat ride to Kuala Tahan

claim: Cameron Highlands to Taman Negara (Kuala Tahan) van-ferry/minivan tickets from about US$20.
quote: Cameron Highlands to Taman Negara (Kuala Tahan) - van-ferry, minivan, bus tickets from US$20

claim: Taman Negara to Kuala Besut jetty minivan: RM130 (RM150 from 1 Apr 2026), departs Kuala Tahan 08:00, arrives Kuala Besut ~16:30, 7-8hr with two rest stops.
quote: RM 130.00... RM 150.00 (effective April 1, 2026)... Departure: 8:00 AM from Kuala Tahan... Arrival: 4:30 PM at Kuala Besut Jetty... 7-8 hours with two rest stops

claim: Taman Negara (Kuala Tahan) to Kuala Besut minivan/bus tickets from about US$9.
quote: Taman Negara (Kuala Tahan) to Kuala Besut - minivan, bus tickets from US$9

claim: Jungle Railway runs Gemas-Tumpat through Pahang/Kelantan; Jerantut is the station for Taman Negara; modern air-conditioned DMU shuttles plus a daily JB-Tumpat sleeper.
quote: Jerantut in Pahang is another popular access point as it is the station to or from Taman Negara

claim: The Jungle Railway is a scenic slow ride; the Gua Musang-area section through forest is the most scenic.
quote: the most scenic sections

claim: Crossing the Sungai Tembeling by local sampan from Kuala Tahan to the park HQ / Mutiara resort costs about RM1 per person.
quote: RM1 per person

claim: A quick sampan crossing of the river separates Kuala Tahan village from the park HQ; it costs RM1.
quote: it costs RM1 to take a boat across

claim: Activity prices: Lata Berkoh boat RM450/boat (max 4), Kuala Trenggan rapids RM70/pax, night boat cruise RM70/pax, Orang Asli village RM100/pax, night jungle walk RM50/pax (all min 4).
quote: Lata Berkoh: RM450 PER BOAT FOR MAXIMUM 4 PEOPLE... Rapids Shooting to Kuala Trenggan: RM70 per adult/child... Orang Asli Village Visit: RM100... Night Jungle Walk: RM50

claim: Gua Telinga (Ear Cave) is reached by boat downstream; it has been closed to the public since May 2023 for safety reasons.
quote: as of May 2023, this cave has been closed to the public due to safety factor

claim: Kuala Gandah Elephant Sanctuary runs as a full-day tour ex-KL (often combined with fireflies), and lies on the KL-Taman Negara road corridor.
quote: Elephant Sanctuary and Fireflies Day Tour (ex-KL)

claim: Kuala Gandah Elephant Sanctuary is in Lancang, Pahang, ~110km / ~1.5-2.5hr from KL; entry is free as it is government-run.
quote: approximately 110 km... from Kuala Lumpur... Entrance to the sanctuary is free

claim: Kenong Rimba Park sits on Taman Negara's eastern/northern fringe, covers 128 sq km, has limestone caves and waterfalls, and is accessed via Kuala Lipis with a compulsory guide.
quote: located at the fringe of Taman Negara on its eastern and northern boundaries... 128 square kilometres

claim: Kenong Rimba is explored on 1-6 day jungle treks organised from Kuala Lipis; guides are compulsory.
quote: explored on one- to six-day jungle treks organised from Kuala Lipis

claim: Kuala Lipis is a former Pahang state capital with colonial-era buildings along Jalan Bukit Bius, reachable by the Jungle Railway.
quote: Kuala Lipis was the capital of the state of Pahang... old style colonial buildings up the hills along Jalan Bukit Bius

claim: Best window is the dry season ~Feb-Sep, with Mar-May ideal for wildlife and trails; the NE monsoon Nov-Feb brings heavy rain, high rivers and trickier/less safe river crossings.
quote: March through May is widely considered the best time... Heavy rain from the monsoon season hits Taman Negara from November to February, making jungle trekking and river crossings tricky and less safe

claim: In early June 2026 the EUR/MYR rate was roughly 4.6-4.7 ringgit per euro.
quote: as of June 5, 2026, the EUR to MYR rate was approximately 4.6399
